name: Machu Picchu (Lost City of the Incas)
description: Spectacular 15th-century royal mountain citadel in the Peruvian Andes, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Constructed as a royal estate for Emperor Pachacuti atop a mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level. Abandoned around the time of the Spanish conquest and brought to global attention by Hiram Bingham in 1911.
construction: Constructed with dry-stone ashlar masonry where huge polished granite blocks fit together seamlessly without mortar, resilient to powerful Andean earthquakes.
architecture: Features over 200 agricultural terraces, residential compounds, ceremonial temples (Intihuatana astronomical stone), and cascading stone water fountains.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
currentStatus: Standing majestically preserved above the Urubamba Valley in Peru.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, representing the pinnacle of Incan stone masonry and harmonious mountain urban planning.
